publisher: Each state's code (municipal and county law) and the Council of the District of Columbia's rules
table: The enacting clause state law prescribes for a town's or county's ordinances, and the numbering, by place
title: Local ordinance enacting clauses and numbering by state, 2026
universe: The general law most towns and counties of each place follow when their own charter says nothing; charter and home-rule places set their own (the place's code of ordinances is the record for those).
geography: state or territory, keyed by postal code; all 56 places
limits: A SOURCED row quotes the state statute as fetched on Oct 23, 2026; {place}, {body} and {kind} mark the blanks the statute leaves for the town's name, its governing body and its kind (city, town, village). A statute often covers one class of city only (appliesTo); other classes and charter cities may differ. `kinds` names the kinds of place (city, town, village, county) a clause that quotes a statute covers; a statute that gives another kind its own words is a separate entry under alsoSourced, as Nebraska's village clause is, and the check script fails a clause whose scope its words or its quote do not support. An ESTIMATED row is the national default from bill-forms.json, or (Texas) a statute read from a reproduction because the official page renders only by script. The clauses are research for the Words session: they reach no player text until the English engine's banks take them up. No statute read prescribes a local ordinance numbering; only the D.C. Council's rules do.
readBy: scripts/research/legislature-local-rules-check.ts (shape check; reports which places differ from the national default). No engine reads it yet: gov-legislature-local-rules-by-place (bodyNumbering in src/core2/legislature-bill-form.ts) and words-local-enacting-clause-by-state (the English engine's legislation bank) are the items that will.

numbering.appliesTo: the Council of the District of Columbia
numbering.quote: The Secretary shall assign 2-part numbers to Council documents identified in subsection (b) of this section in the order of introduction, filing, adoption, or approval. The first part of the number consists of the current Council Period, and the second part consists of a consecutive serial number beginning with the number "1" in each Council Period.
